literal: " Shenwu greatly rejoiced and summoned the empress and Wenxiang.
idiomatic: " Shenwu greatly rejoiced and summoned the empress and Wenxiang.

literal: Wuming Empress from afar saw Shenwu—one step one knock of the head.
idiomatic: Wuming Empress from afar saw Shenwu—one step one knock of the head.

literal: Wenxiang both bowed and advanced; father, son, husband and wife wept together—then as at first.
idiomatic: Wenxiang both bowed and advanced; father, son, husband and wife wept together—then as at first.

literal: Shenwu then set wine: "He who preserved me father and son was Sima Ziru."
idiomatic: Shenwu then set wine, "He who preserved me father and son was Sima Ziru."

literal: He granted him one hundred thirty jin of yellow gold; Wenxiang gifted fifty fine horses.
idiomatic: He granted him one hundred thirty jin of yellow gold; Wenxiang gifted fifty fine horses.

literal: Gaoyang Grand Consort You—father Jingzhi was chief clerk of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: Gaoyang Grand Consort You—father Jingzhi was chief clerk of Xiangzhou.

literal: When Shenwu took Ye he wished to take her in;
idiomatic: When Shenwu took Ye he wished to take her in;

literal: Jingzhi did not permit; he was dragged and taken.
idiomatic: Jingzhi did not permit; he was dragged and taken.

literal: Jingzhi soon died.
idiomatic: Jingzhi soon died.

literal: Among all grand consorts You had most moral instruction; princes' and princesses' marriages and betrothals were often put in her charge.
idiomatic: Among all grand consorts You had most moral instruction; princes' and princesses' marriages and betrothals were often put in her charge.

literal: Lady Feng was Zi'ang's younger sister; at first consort of Wei Prince of Rencheng; she married Erzhu Shilong.
idiomatic: Lady Feng was Zi'ang's younger sister; at first consort of Wei Prince of Rencheng; she married Erzhu Shilong.

literal: Shenwu took her in; she bore Princess of Fuyang.
idiomatic: Shenwu took her in; she bore Princess of Fuyang.

literal: Lady Li was Yanshi's younger cousin.
idiomatic: Lady Li was Yanshi's younger cousin.

literal: At first consort of Wei Prince of Chengyang.
idiomatic: At first consort of Wei Prince of Chengyang.

literal: Also Lady Wang bore Prince of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince of Pingyang Yan—both died early and were not grand consorts.
idiomatic: Also Lady Wang bore Prince of Yong'an Jun; Lady Mu bore Prince of Pingyang Yan—both died early and were not grand consorts.

literal: Both died early and were not grand consorts.
idiomatic: Both died early and were not grand consorts.

literal: Wenxiang Jing Empress Yuan was younger sister of Wei Emperor Xiaojing.
idiomatic: Wenxiang Jing Empress Yuan was younger sister of Wei Emperor Xiaojing.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and returned to Wenxiang.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and returned to Wenxiang.

literal: Bearing and virtue both beautiful; harmony and respect fully achieved.
idiomatic: Bearing and virtue both beautiful; harmony and respect fully achieved.

literal: First she bore Prince of Hejian Xiaowan; at the time Wenxiang was heir; on the third day Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and gifted ten thousand bolts of brocade and cloth.
idiomatic: First she bore Prince of Hejian Xiaowan; at the time Wenxiang was heir; on the third day Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and gifted ten thousand bolts of brocade and cloth.

literal: The heir declined; he asked to receive together the nobles' ritual gifts—then ten rooms were all full.
idiomatic: The heir declined; he asked to receive together the nobles' ritual gifts—then ten rooms were all full.

literal: Next she bore two princesses.
idiomatic: Next she bore two princesses.

literal: When Wenxuan received abdication, she was honored Wenxiang Empress and dwelt at Jingde Palace.
idiomatic: When Wenxuan received abdication, she was honored Wenxiang Empress and dwelt at Jingde Palace.

literal: By the sixth year of Tianbao Wenxuan gradually fell into mad frenzy; he moved her to Gaoyang's residence and took her treasury, saying: "My elder brother once violated my wife—now I must repay."
idiomatic: By the sixth year of Tianbao Wenxuan gradually fell into mad frenzy; he moved her to Gaoyang's residence and took her treasury, saying, "My elder brother once violated my wife—now I must repay."

literal: Then he violated the empress.
idiomatic: Then he violated the empress.

literal: Gao women, consorts—without regard for near or far—all he had attendants disorderly join them before him.
idiomatic: Gao women, consorts—without regard for near or far—all he had attendants disorderly join them before him.

literal: With hemp as a rope he ordered Princess of Wei Ande ride atop; men pushed and drew her.
idiomatic: With hemp as a rope he ordered Princess of Wei Ande ride atop; men pushed and drew her.

literal: Also he ordered barbarians cruelly to humiliate them.
idiomatic: Also he ordered barbarians cruelly to humiliate them.

literal: The emperor also exposed himself to show the crowd below.
idiomatic: The emperor also exposed himself to show the crowd below.

literal: Under Wuping the empress died and was attached-buried at Yiping Tomb.
idiomatic: Under Wuping the empress died and was attached-buried at Yiping Tomb.

literal: Princess of Langye, name Yuyi, was younger uterine sister of Wei Prince of Gaoyang Bin.
idiomatic: Princess of Langye, name Yuyi, was younger uterine sister of Wei Prince of Gaoyang Bin.

literal: At first her teeth were not seen; she was Sun Teng's courtesan; Teng again abandoned her.
idiomatic: At first her teeth were not seen; she was Sun Teng's courtesan; Teng again abandoned her.

literal: Wenxiang met her on the road, delighted and took her in; she received exceptional favor; he memorialized the Wei emperor to enfeoff her.
idiomatic: Wenxiang met her on the road, delighted and took her in; she received exceptional favor; he memorialized the Wei emperor to enfeoff her.

literal: Wenxiang told Cui Jishu: "You always sought beauty for me—not as good as my finding one utterly unique.
idiomatic: Wenxiang told Cui Jishu, "You always sought beauty for me—not as good as my finding one utterly unique.

literal: Cui Kui will surely come with straight remonstrance—I also have means to wait for him."
idiomatic: Cui Kui will surely come with straight remonstrance—I also have means to wait for him."

literal: When Kui reported affairs, Wenxiang no longer lent him a pleasant face.
idiomatic: When Kui reported affairs, Wenxiang no longer lent him a pleasant face.

literal: After three days Kui carried a memorial and dropped it before him.
idiomatic: After three days Kui carried a memorial and dropped it before him.

literal: Wenxiang asked: "What use is this?"
idiomatic: Wenxiang asked, "What use is this?"

literal: Kui fearfully said: "I have not yet obtained access to the princess."
idiomatic: Kui fearfully said, "I have not yet obtained access to the princess."

literal: Wenxiang greatly rejoiced, took Kui's arm and entered to see her.
idiomatic: Wenxiang greatly rejoiced, took Kui's arm and entered to see her.

literal: Jishu told others: "Cui Kui always resented my flattery; before the grand marshal he always said my uncle ought to be killed.
idiomatic: Jishu told others, "Cui Kui always resented my flattery; before the grand marshal he always said my uncle ought to be killed.

literal: When he himself played the flatterer, his body exceeded mine."
idiomatic: When he himself played the flatterer, his body exceeded mine."

literal: Yuyi's uterine elder sister Jingyi had first married Attendant-in-Chief Cui Kuo; Wenxiang also favored her—both were enfeoffed princess.
idiomatic: Yuyi's uterine elder sister Jingyi had first married Attendant-in-Chief Cui Kuo; Wenxiang also favored her—both were enfeoffed princess.

literal: Kuo father and son thereby received extraordinary promotion; rewards were very thick.
idiomatic: Kuo father and son thereby received extraordinary promotion; rewards were very thick.

literal: Wenxuan Empress Li, taboo name Zue, was daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Wenxuan Empress Li, taboo name Zue, was daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao commandery.

literal: Bearing and virtue were very beautiful.
idiomatic: Bearing and virtue were very beautiful.

literal: At first she was consort of Duke of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: At first she was consort of Duke of Taiyuan.

literal: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace,
idiomatic: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace,

literal: Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said Han women could not be mother of the realm—one should again choose a beautiful match.
idiomatic: Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said Han women could not be mother of the realm—one should again choose a beautiful match.

literal: Yang Yin firmly requested following Han and Wei precedent, not changing the original consort.
idiomatic: Yang Yin firmly requested following Han and Wei precedent, not changing the original consort.

literal: Dezheng still firmly requested deposing the empress and establishing Duan zhaoyi, wishing to bind merit-nobles' support.
idiomatic: Dezheng still firmly requested deposing the empress and establishing Duan zhaoyi, wishing to bind merit-nobles' support.

literal: The emperor ultimately did not follow and established the empress.
idiomatic: The emperor ultimately did not follow and established the empress.

literal: The emperor liked beating pin and attendants—even to killing; only toward the empress alone was ritual respect kept.
idiomatic: The emperor liked beating pin and attendants—even to killing; only toward the empress alone was ritual respect kept.

literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was changed to Kehedun Empress.
idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was changed to Kehedun Empress.

literal: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she was demoted to Zhaoxin Palace, title Zhaoxin Empress.
idiomatic: When Xiaozhao took the throne, she was demoted to Zhaoxin Palace, title Zhaoxin Empress.

literal: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into disorder, saying: "If you do not permit me, I will kill your son."
idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into disorder, saying, "If you do not permit me, I will kill your son."

literal: The empress feared and yielded.
idiomatic: The empress feared and yielded.

literal: Later she was pregnant; Prince of Taiyuan Shaode came to the pavilion and could not see her.
idiomatic: Later she was pregnant; Prince of Taiyuan Shaode came to the pavilion and could not see her.

literal: Angrily he said: "Does the child not know?
idiomatic: Angrily he said, "Does the child not know?

literal: Elder sister's belly is big—therefore she does not see the child."
idiomatic: Elder sister's belly is big—therefore she does not see the child."

literal: When the empress heard she was greatly ashamed; from this she bore girls and did not raise them.
idiomatic: When the empress heard she was greatly ashamed; from this she bore girls and did not raise them.

literal: The emperor with a bare blade cursed: "You killed my daughter—why should I not kill your son?"
idiomatic: The emperor with a bare blade cursed, "You killed my daughter—why should I not kill your son?"

literal: Before the empress he built and killed Shaode.
idiomatic: Before the empress he built and killed Shaode.

literal: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier, stripped the empress and beat her disorderly; she cried to Heaven without end.
idiomatic: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier, stripped the empress and beat her disorderly; she cried to Heaven without end.

literal: He packed her in a silk bag; blood dripped soaking; he cast her into the canal water; after long while she revived; an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.
idiomatic: He packed her in a silk bag; blood dripped soaking; he cast her into the canal water; after a long while she revived; an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.

literal: The empress by nature loved Buddhist law; therefore she became a nun.
idiomatic: The empress by nature loved Buddhist law; therefore she became a nun.

literal: When Qi fell, she entered Guanzhong; under Sui she could return to Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: When Qi fell, she entered Guanzhong; under Sui she could return to Zhao commandery.

literal: Duan zhaoyi was Shao's younger sister.
idiomatic: Duan zhaoyi was Shao's younger sister.

literal: On the wedding evening Shao's wife Lady Yuan performed vulgar teasing of the son-in-law for Wenxuan; Wenxuan harbored resentment.
idiomatic: On the wedding evening Shao's wife Lady Yuan performed vulgar teasing of the son-in-law for Wenxuan; Wenxuan harbored resentment.

literal: Later because of anger he told Shao: "I will kill your wife!"
idiomatic: Later because of anger he told Shao, "I will kill your wife!"

literal: Lady Yuan feared and hid at Empress Dowager Lou's house; through Wenxuan's age she dared not come out.
idiomatic: Lady Yuan feared and hid at Empress Dowager Lou's house; through Wenxuan's age she dared not come out.

literal: Zhaoyi had talent and beauty together; courtesy nearly equaled the principal wife.
idiomatic: Zhaoyi had talent and beauty together; courtesy nearly equaled the principal wife.

literal: Under the later lord she remarried Director of Records Tang Yong.
idiomatic: Under the later lord she remarried Director of Records Tang Yong.

literal: Lady Wang pin was a man of Langye.
idiomatic: Lady Wang pin was a man of Langye.

literal: The pin's elder sister had first married Cui Xiu; Wenxuan favored both.
idiomatic: The pin's elder sister had first married Cui Xiu; Wenxuan favored both.

literal: Repeatedly he lowered himself to their husband's house and promoted Xiu to Masters of Writing lang.
idiomatic: Repeatedly he lowered himself to their husband's house and promoted Xiu to Masters of Writing lang.

literal: Lady Xue pin was originally a singing-house girl.
idiomatic: Lady Xue pin was originally a singing-house girl.

literal: At fourteen or fifteen she was liked by Prince of Qinghe Yue.
idiomatic: At fourteen or fifteen she was liked by Prince of Qinghe Yue.

literal: Her father asked to enter the inner palace; she was greatly favored.
idiomatic: Her father asked to enter the inner palace; she was greatly favored.

literal: Her elder sister also both entered to attend.
idiomatic: Her elder sister also both entered to attend.

literal: Later Wenxuan learned she had earlier communicated with Yue; also her father begged Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Later Wenxuan learned she had earlier communicated with Yue; also her father begged Minister of Works.

literal: The emperor greatly angered; first he sawed and killed her elder sister.
idiomatic: The emperor greatly angered; first he sawed and killed her elder sister.

literal: Lady Xue pin was then pregnant; at delivery she was also executed with the rest.
idiomatic: Lady Xue pin was then pregnant; at delivery she was also executed with the rest.

literal: Wucheng Empress Hu was daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.
idiomatic: Wucheng Empress Hu was daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.

literal: Her mother was daughter of Fanyang Lu Daoyue.
idiomatic: Her mother was daughter of Fanyang Lu Daoyue.

literal: At first pregnancy a Hu monk came to the door saying: "In this house's bottle-gourd is a moon."
idiomatic: At first pregnancy a Hu monk came to the door saying, "In this house's bottle-gourd is a moon."

literal: Then the empress was born.
idiomatic: Then the empress was born.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was chosen as Prince of Changgung's consort.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao she was chosen as Prince of Changgung's consort.

literal: On the day the later lord was born, an owl cried on the birth canopy.
idiomatic: On the day the later lord was born, an owl cried on the birth canopy.

literal: When Wucheng died she was honored Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: When Wucheng died she was honored empress dowager.

literal: Lu the wet-nurse and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince of Zhao Chen; they sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as prefects.
idiomatic: Lu the wet-nurse and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince of Zhao Chen; they sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as prefects.

literal: He and Lu fawned on the empress dowager to the utmost.
idiomatic: He and Lu fawned on the empress dowager to the utmost.

literal: At first under Wucheng the empress had indecent dealings with various eunuchs.
idiomatic: At first under Wucheng the empress had indecent dealings with various eunuchs.

literal: Wucheng favored He Shikai.
idiomatic: Wucheng favored He Shikai.

literal: Each time with the empress he played spear-game—thereby he communicated in adultery with the empress.
idiomatic: Each time with the empress he played spear-game—thereby he communicated in adultery with the empress.

literal: From after Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples; also she communicated with the monk Tanxian.
idiomatic: From after Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples; also she communicated with the monk Tanxian.

literal: She spread gold money under Tanxian's ordination platform; also hung a treasure-adorned Hu bed on Tanxian's room wall—what Wucheng in life had used.
idiomatic: She spread gold money under Tanxian's ordination platform; also hung a treasure-adorned Hu bed on Tanxian's room wall—what Wucheng in life had used.

literal: Then she placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, under pretext of hearing lectures—day and night she slept with Tanxian.
idiomatic: Then she placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, under pretext of hearing lectures—day and night she slept with Tanxian.

literal: She made Tanxian Director of Illuminated Mystery.
idiomatic: She made Tanxian Director of Illuminated Mystery.

literal: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager to tease Tanxian—even calling her the Supreme One.
idiomatic: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager to tease Tanxian—even calling her the Supreme One.
